 NBA Rejects Sabonis Investigation Claims as Trade Rumors Grow

 Questions surrounding Domantas Sabonis ' future in Sacramento have intensified following a difficult start to the NBA season, while an unsubstantiated investigation claim has added another controversy to the three-time All-Star's situation. As of November 18, 2026, the NBA had issued no statement indicating that Sabonis was under investigation following his scoreless performance against the Orlando Magic.
 According to BasketballNews, Sabonis played 24 minutes against Orlando on Tuesday, attempting just two field goals and missing both. He also missed two free throws but contributed two rebounds and five assists.
 Advertisement 
 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 No established news outlet cited in the report had confirmed an investigation, and no official league announcement supported the allegation. The available information instead points to injury recovery, changes in Sacramento's offensive approach, and growing uncertainty about Sabonis' future.
 Also Read 
 Domantas Sabonis Dismisses Offseason Trade Rumors as Sacramento Kings Prepare 
 The discussion gained momentum after NBA analyst Kevin O'Connor wrote on X that Sabonis "doesn't want to be there." The phrase "quiet quitting" subsequently became associated with the debate over his performances and commitment to the struggling Kings.
 However, the coverage identifies no credible evidence connecting Sabonis to suspicious activity or an official league inquiry. A separate investigation involving Toronto Raptors forward Jontay Porter in 2024 has provided historical context for the speculation, but the circumstances surrounding the two players are different.
 In Porter's case, unusual activity surrounding his individual performances preceded an NBA investigation. The league subsequently banned him for life. No comparable evidence has been reported in Sabonis' situation.
 Also Read 
 Kings Look to Leaky Black to Complement Darius Acuff Jr. 
 NBA commissioner-related scrutiny of Sacramento previously involved head coach Doug Christie after an intentional-foul controversy involving Seth Curry and the Golden State Warriors. The league's statement concluded that Christie "made no intentional effort to give the Warriors a shooting foul."
 Meanwhile, Sacramento's disappointing 1-12 record has strengthened speculation about a possible roster overhaul. According to reporting by The Athletic's Sam Amick, the Kings are willing to consider offers for almost every player except rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr.
 Sabonis has attracted attention from potential trade partners, including the Charlotte Hornets and Toronto Raptors, ahead of the February 11 trade deadline. His contract remains a significant obstacle, with $45.4 million owed this season and $48.6 million in 2027-28.
 Also Read 
 Damian Lillard Backs Darius Acuff Jr. Amid Kings Struggles 
 The financial commitment presents particular challenges for Charlotte. Although the Hornets possess a $40.77 million traded player exception created through the LaMelo Ball deal, that amount cannot cover Sabonis' current salary. NBA collective bargaining rules also prevent the team from combining that exception with outgoing player salaries to absorb one contract.
 A potential acquisition would therefore require Charlotte to surrender multiple player contracts or other assets. The long-term financial implications are also significant because Brandon Miller's five-year, $209 million extension begins in 2027-28, with an annual value of approximately $36 million.
 Sabonis has also faced physical challenges following the injury and surgery that sidelined him for most of last season. According to BasketballNews, ankle problems related to that injury reportedly kept him out of the game immediately preceding the Orlando matchup.
 Also Read 
 Simmons Proposes Jokic Trade as Rockets Target NBA Star 
 Although Sabonis has said he is "shocked" by the appearance of his name in offseason trade reports, Sacramento's changing offensive structure has reduced his role. The Kings have increasingly directed their scoring through Acuff Jr. and Zach LaVine, leaving Sabonis with fewer opportunities to initiate offense.
 His five assists against Orlando reflected that reduced scoring involvement, while his limited playing time followed a recent absence. The NBA has not announced an investigation into his performance, and the claims remain unsupported by credible evidence.
